title: smart-routing-fallback-incident-breadcrumbs-arjun
content:
Context / summary:
- Personal scratchpad capturing breadcrumbs from the smart routing + fallback policy incident affecting us-west1 -> regional failover on 2025-08-02.
- High level: spike in 5xx and latency from hosted-api requests routed to us-west1. Smart router started triggering fallback policies; some customers saw expanded regional failover to us-east1, others got errors saying "no compatible model variant".
- Goal: capture commands run, outputs, quick hypotheses, and next steps for a proper postmortem draft.

Timeline (local times):
- 2025-08-02 09:12: first alerts: rate of 5xx from us-west1 (alerts: route-error-rate > 2% for 10m).
- 2025-08-02 09:16: Ops runbook step 1 executed: check router health and pool capacity.
- 2025-08-02 09:21: Router started marking endpoints unhealthy; fallback policy kicked in at 09:22.
- 2025-08-02 09:30: Some customers saw "fallback failed: no compatible model variant found" (observed in support tickets).
- 2025-08-02 09:45: Manual mitigation: tightened fallback policy (disabled region-pref override) + restarted router service. Partial recovery by 10:05.

Commands / queries tried (most useful ones):
- Check router errors:
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" "https://admin.redwood.internal/v1/router/status?region=us-west1" | jq
  -> response: { "healthy_endpoints": 2, "unhealthy": ["rtr-07", "rtr-09"], "fallback_policy": "region-fallback-v2" }

- Get pod restarts / logs from k8s for router:
  kubectl -n routing get pods -l app=smart-router -o wide
  kubectl -n routing logs smart-router-07 --since=1h | egrep -i "error|warn|fallback|timeout" -A3 -B1
  -> observed repeated: "ERROR: heartbeat timeout to pool us-west1-gpu (latency=1200ms)" and "INFO: triggering fallback for request id=..."

- Check model server status in us-west1:
  curl -s http://model-orchestrator.us-west1.internal/health | jq
  -> status: "degraded", active_workers: 6/8, kv_cache_miss_rate: 0.18, avg_inference_latency_ms: 750
  docker ps on nodes showed model-quantizer restart loops on 2 nodes (OOM killed?)

- Review routing decision logs for a sample request id (request id truncated):
  SELECT * FROM routing_decisions WHERE req_id LIKE '20250802-%' ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 50;
  -> log snippet: "decision: route->us-west1, endpoint unhealthy, fallback->try-us-east1: variant-match-failed"

- Admin API used to toggle fallback config:
  POST /admin/config/fallback -d '{"policy": "region-fallback-v2", "max_hops": 1, "allow_variant_mismatch": false }'
  -> Swagger response 200 but behavior unchanged until router restart.

Observed error snippets (copied):
- "FallbackPolicyError: no compatible model variant found for requested model: rw-model-1-large"
- "RouteError: No healthy endpoints in region us-west1 after 3 retries"
- "heartbeat timeout to pool us-west1-gpu" repeated ~every 30s
- Kernel OOM / process exit in quantizer: "Killed process 2345 (model-quantizer) due to OOM"

Hypotheses (ranked quickly):
1) Underlying model-serving instability in us-west1 (OOMs on quantizer causing workers to die) causing increased latency and unhealthy endpoints -> router triggers fallback.
   Evidence: kube logs show OOM kills + model server health degraded + higher avg_inference_latency_ms.
2) Fallback policy misconfiguration: allow_variant_mismatch=false + strict variant matching prevents successful failover even when a compatible quantized variant exists in other region.
   Evidence: routing_decisions show "variant-match-failed" even though model catalog lists a quantized variant in us-east1. Maybe mismatch in model tags between catalog and router cache.
3) Router stale cache / config propagation lag: admin API returned 200 for config update but router didn't pick it up until restart.
   Evidence: change visible only after restart.
4) Cloud provider networking hiccup in us-west1 zone causing heartbeat timeouts to pool.
   Evidence: heartbeat timeouts across multiple hosts, but cloud provider reported no broad outage (need to confirm).

Immediate mitigations attempted and results:
- Brought up extra capacity in us-west1 (scaled model workers + added 2 extra gpu nodes) at 09:38 -> helped reduce latency after 20m.
- Restarted smart-router pods at 09:42 -> router picked up new config and fallback behavior normalized by ~10:05.
- Temporarily relaxed fallback policy (allow_variant_mismatch=true) for a few customers to reduce errors; this allowed cross-region variants to be used but introduced small quality variance.
- Opened node-level incident (K8S-4728) for OOMs in quantizer; memory profiling requested.

What I ran that failed to change behavior:
- Hot-reloading fallback config via admin API (POST /admin/config/fallback) — returned 200 but router did not apply until restart.
- Toggling regional routing weight in admin console — didn't help while model servers were OOMing.

Logs / snippets to preserve for postmortem:
- Router logs (smart-router-07) 09:12-10:30: heartbeat timeout messages, fallback triggers, variant-match-failed entries. (saved to S3: s3://incidents/INC-2025-113/router-logs-20250802.tar.gz)
- Kube events for model-serving ns: node OOM, container restarts (k8s-logs saved).
- Sample request traces (trace ids list copied to incident doc).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Why did admin API not propagate config to router without restart? Is there a missed push/long-poll in the router config sync? (Owner: Ethan)
- Why was variant matching failing even though model catalog lists compatible quantized variants in us-east1? Potential tag mismatch between model-catalog and router cache (Owner: Maya).
- Root cause of quantizer OOM: spike in concurrent seq lengths? memory regression after recent quantizer change (PR #389) — need memprof and bisect (Owner: Arjun).
- Confirm cloud provider network events for the us-west1 zone on 2025-08-02 09:00-10:00 (Owner: Riley).

Next steps (short term):
- Create a postmortem draft with timeline, impact, mitigations, and action items (this doc will be the starting point).
- Add a test to our staging to validate fallback config hot-reload (to prevent need for restarts for config changes). (Ethan)
- Add an integration test for variant matching across regions to ensure tag canonicalization between model-catalog and router cache. (Maya)
- Memory profiling of quantizer binary + possibly revert PR #389 if it correlates. (Arjun)
- Communication: notify affected customers with timeline + mitigation summary (CS to confirm message).

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep raw command outputs in incident S3 bucket; they will be noisy but useful.
- This doc is rough — will move to shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/incidents/INC-2025-113-postmortem when first draft ready.
- Save key logs and set retention 90d for post-incident analysis.

Random breadcrumbs (may be redundant):
- Observed one support ticket where user cutover was impacted because their pinned model version wasn't available in fallback region. Need to clarify docs around pinned model behavior during regional failover.
- Consider a metric: fallback-success-rate by region and by model-variant to detect variant-mismatch early.

If I forget later: TODO add timeline of exact customer-impact windows (extract from support tickets + telemetry) and estimate number of requests failed.

-- Arjun
